comparison: Perfect alignment on training protocol claims (C13-C25). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes transparency and clear documentation of attrition rates, while peer reviewers acknowledge the strong fundamental design but note the 40% attrition rate as a limitation requiring potential optimization.

Perfect alignment on place cell property claims (C84-C86). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the novel finding of increased place cell numbers and replication of place field narrowing, while acknowledging small sample size (n=8). Peer reviewers accept these findings as validation of the paradigm's utility for exploring memory dynamics.

Perfect alignment on limitation claims (C101-C108). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval characterizes these as appropriately discussed and transparent limitations. Peer reviewers acknowledge the authors' self-assessment of limitations, particularly highlighting the extended training and attrition rate as a weakness.

Strong alignment on Paradigm 1 behavioral findings (C35-C43). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes statistical rigor with paired t-tests and clear p-values. Peer reviewers explicitly endorse Paradigm 1 as 'most promising' with greatest conditioned freezing (~40%) and good context discrimination (delta ~15-20%).

Strong alignment on remapping findings (C81-C83). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the finding that remapping occurred in both VRs differs from some prior studies. Peer reviewers validate findings as largely replicating previous work in freely moving subjects, acknowledging the difference that VR CFC led to remapping of control environment as noteworthy.

Strong alignment on paradigm design claims (C26-C29) with partial overlap on shock protocol (C30-C34). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval describes these as straightforward experimental design descriptions. Peer reviewers explicitly discussed the three paradigm variations and accepted shock parameters without critique.

Moderate alignment on shock protocol claims (C30-C34). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes documentation of shock parameters and immediate running response as evidence of proper apparatus function. Peer reviewers accepted experimental design and shock parameters without critique.

Alignment on individual variability and parameter optimization claims (C44-C46). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate contextualization of variability with citations and acknowledges relatively small sample sizes for parameter exploration. Peer reviewers accepted parameter-testing results as valid contributions to paradigm development.

Alignment on temporal dynamics claims (C47-C49). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval documents rapid extinction with LME models while noting decreasing sample sizes across recall days. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted these findings as part of setting initial parameters for paradigm optimization.

Partial alignment on Paradigm 2 findings (C50-C55), but divergent evaluations. OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED, noting first lap effects were statistically significant while average freezing was not. Peer reviewers evaluate as UNCERTAIN, stating 'Version 2 showed no clear evidence of learning' and that single lap effects are 'not useful for many neural circuit questions.'

Alignment on Paradigm 2 rapid extinction claims (C56-C62). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED with detailed statistical documentation. Peer reviewers evaluate as UNCERTAIN overall for Paradigm 2, criticizing lack of robust average freezing effects despite acknowledging the rapid extinction pattern.

Strong alignment on Paradigm 3 findings (C63-C69). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes improved discrimination over Paradigm 2 with strongest average freezing effects. Peer reviewers acknowledge Paradigm 3's improvements and greater freezing/slower extinction than version 2, while noting room for further optimization.

Alignment on Paradigm 3 temporal dynamics claims (C70-C73). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval documents maintenance of discrimination and delayed extinction through LME analysis. Peer reviewers accepted these findings as part of Paradigm 3's improved performance over Paradigm 2.

Alignment on methodological advantages claim (C93). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes comparison to prior air-puff methods and freezing as conditioned response. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledged this advance addresses limitations where lick suppression doesn't allow comparison with freely moving animals.

Alignment on neutral environment choice effects claim (C90). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this is supported by comparisons across paradigms. Peer reviewers explicitly discussed familiarity variations and comparative effectiveness, accepting that environmental familiarity affects fear discrimination.

Alignment on additional defensive behaviors claim (C89). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes documentation in videos and behavioral traces. Peer reviewers acknowledged the paradigm produces freezing as conditioned response, implicitly accepting the behavioral observations.

Alignment on summary freezing behavior claims (C87-C88). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval states these summary claims are well-supported by detailed results. Peer reviewers' editor assessment noted 'solid evidence supports the claim' that head-fixed mice exhibited freezing consistent with freely moving animals.

Alignment on place cell findings summary claim (C92). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval states this is supported by imaging data. Peer reviewers validated the paradigm's utility for exploring memory dynamics through hippocampal neuron remapping observations.

Alignment on experimental parameters effects claim (C91). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes support from cross-paradigm comparisons. Peer reviewers discussed paradigm variations and their differential effectiveness, implicitly accepting parameter effects.

Alignment on multi-photon imaging background claims (C1-C5). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval characterizes these as well-supported established knowledge. Peer reviewers accepted the rationale without challenge, acknowledging the approach enables multiphoton imaging during traditionally freely-moving behaviors.

Alignment on traditional CFC paradigm background claims (C6-C12). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate documentation of prior work and motivation for current study. Peer reviewers accepted this scientific context without challenge.

Alignment on hippocampal function background claims (C74-C80). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval characterizes these as well-supported by extensive citations that appropriately motivate imaging experiments. Peer reviewers accepted this established scientific context.

Alignment on physiological measurement capabilities claims (C94-C95). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this is a stated advantage supported by citations though not extensively demonstrated. Peer reviewers accepted the rationale for the approach's technical capabilities.

Alignment on engram cells and technical capabilities claims (C96-C100). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate citations and discussion of differences from other studies. Peer reviewers accepted this background and technical context without challenge.
